summary: At fork head 896bef31e74af42812f4b5ba880450dcad0f6815 (re-verified live at filing; clean clone). ASYNC REPAIR VERIFIED: ProbeGracefulRejectionClientTest passes 14/14 in three consecutive --rerun-tasks runs at seed 17764C0DE (previously 13/14 in full-class runs); the new early completion in HttpJettySolrClient publishes the GracefulShutdownRejectionException before body processing, and no failure chain, leak symptom, or IO-thread completion artifact appears in any run. Tidy: zero changes. ROOT CHECK FAILS at a newly reached leg: :solr:core:validateLogCalls reports 4 violations in ProbeGracefulMultiShardTest.java (lines 275, 305, 353, 396; log calls must be parameterized or guarded). The r2 logger-idiom repair cleared validateSourcePatterns, which is what unblocked this leg. PACKAGED DIAGNOSIS, the r2 question answered: by default the packaged server has NO rejection window at all, for a wiring reason. bin/solr adds --module=graceful only when the environment variable SOLR_JETTY_GRACEFUL=true (bin/solr line ~305, default false); my r2 attempts and r3 attempts 1-3 ran without it, so jetty-graceful.xml never applied: no GracefulShutdownHandler in the chain, Server stopTimeout 0 (log line 'Stopped oejs.Server{STOPPING}[12.1.14,sto=0]'), connector stopped 11 ms after the ShutdownMonitor stop command, and 81/81 fresh-connection polls during stop received connection failure, zero HTTP responses, zero markers, even with a real working collection (created via the Collections API; select verified 200) and four in-flight trickling uploads, which were aborted mid-body. This corrects the r2 receipt, which recorded the wiring as unconditionally present. WITH SOLR_JETTY_GRACEFUL=true the window exists and is exactly as wide as designed: stop took 6.38 s (5 s stopTimeout plus teardown), uploads were held for the window and cut at JVM exit when still unfinished, new TCP connections were still refused from the first moment (81/81), BUT a request sent on an EXISTING keep-alive connection 0.55 s into the window received HTTP 503 with header 'X-Solr-Graceful-Shutdown: rejected' (keep-alive poll 9, 18:17:43.222 UTC; server log shows the stop command at 18:17:43.021 and JVM exit at 18:17:48.448). So the marked rejection is reachable by real clients, which pool keep-alive connections, but only on already-open connections; a client opening a new connection during the window sees connection-refused, a different failure path. MINIMAL CORRECTION for the implementation worker to judge: the feature as shipped in this branch is inert in the default packaged start; either enable the graceful module by default in bin/solr or document SOLR_JETTY_GRACEFUL=true as required wherever the client retry behavior is described. No source was modified or pushed by this diagnostic.
